title: World.worldTime / World.fastForward: no writer is statically reachable in libApplication
question: the live original advances World.worldTime at 20 units per real second while World.fastForward reads 1 (LIVE_WORLD_CLOCK.md), yet the library appears to contain no code that writes either field. This artifact records every mechanism excluded, how, and what is left open.

live_premise_recheck.why: the project has seen 79 __objc_ivar cells rewritten at runtime, which would invalidate every offset-based reading. Re-read live before drawing conclusions.
live_premise_recheck.verdict: premise holds - the readings are valid

exclusions.result: World.worldTime: 3 references all READS. World.fastForward: 1 reference, the ldrsb read in its own getter. 0 writes.

exclusions.how: sweep of store-shaped words over the whole code window, capstone-confirmed
exclusions.result: 440 hits, every one a stack slot ([sp, #0x648] / [sp, #0x3a4]) or a draw-buffer offset (dozens of -draw: methods write a vertex buffer at 0x648). None is a World field.

exclusions.mechanism: offset materialised into a register first (movw rX,#648 ; add rX,rBase,rX ; str)
exclusions.result: 1 hit, verified FALSE POSITIVE: the base was already object+offset, so the address was (DynamicWorld.dynamicObjects element)+0x288, and the sequence stores a pointer (str) while worldTime is a double.

exclusions.how: all 25 .so in the lib dir grepped for the two names

exclusions.result: no -setWorldTime: and no -setFastForward: exist. fastForward is a DECLARED READONLY PROPERTY ('Tc,R,VfastForward'), which is why the one-line getters share a body.

exclusions.how: the property-name cstring 0xf4fff7 and its attribute cstring
exclusions.result: the name is referenced exactly once - by its own property_t. It is not used as a key literal anywhere.

exclusions.mechanism: a bulk copy into the object (memcpy-family)
exclusions.how: the trampolines were first identified (0x1c2888 / 0x1c2924 / 0x1c2948 are 3-instruction PLT entries all funnelling to 0x1c27c0, a dst/src/len routine), then 4043 call sites classified by destination and immediate length
exclusions.result: immediate lengths are 8 (916), 16 (642), 64 (417), 24, 124 (51)...; copies of length >= 0x100 into a non-stack destination: 21 sites, ZERO in World-family methods. No copy into a World object can reach +648.

exclusions.mechanism: the Java / DEX side via the Apportable bridge
exclusions.how: grepped all four DEX files in the APK
exclusions.result: classes2.dex has 3 'fastForward' strings, and all three are Android platform media API text ('Dead object in fastForward.', 'TRANSACTION_fastForward', an AIDL transaction name in the string table). This was announced as a hit and then corrected: a name match is not an attribution.

incidental_cross_check.observed: copy-size histogram from the same sweep: 64 bytes at 417 call sites, 124 bytes at 51
incidental_cross_check.meaning: independently corroborates two facts pinned by other means: the 64-byte tile record and the 124-byte CraftableItem (the savedict evidence getBytes:length:124).

still_open: a runtime-resolved offset (setValue:forKey: with a key read from data, or object_setIvar with the ivar fetched by name) - invisible to every static sweep by construction
a mechanism outside libApplication that does not name the field (so it does not appear in the string greps)
the scan resolves 20593 of 27155 add-sites and 0 of the trampoline-indirect calls; that residue is not claimed covered
consequence_for_the_replacement: game_engine.cpp maps its sleep state onto fastForward; the STATE and the 20.0 factor are measured, the trigger is not. That mapping stays labelled an inference.
